title: feat(guides): serve encode disaggregation on the vLLM nightly image
body:
## Summary

Move the Coordinator Disaggregation guide and the multimodal Encode Disaggregation
guide (E/PD and E/P/D) from pinned development vLLM images to the upstream vLLM
nightly image. Configure the
[ECCPU Connector](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/ec_cpu_connector/) in its
P2P NIXL mode, with the V2 model runner that it requires. In the Coordinator guide,
replace the Coordinator's CPU render sidecar with a Service that fronts the prefill
model servers. Add CoreWeave overlays for E/PD and E/P/D. Make the vLLM model
servers and the Coordinator pull their moving image tags (`:nightly`, `:main`) on
every start.

The nightly pin is temporary: we expect to move to the vLLM 0.29.0 release image
once it ships, since encoder-cache transfer is not in any released version yet.

## Changes

### Both guides: vLLM nightly image and ECCPU Connector

- **Image:** the `gpu-vllm/nightly` component (`docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`)
  replaces `ghcr.io/revit13/vllm-openai:61e53561a` (Coordinator guide) and the
  `gpu-vllm/ec-connector` component (`ghcr.io/llm-d/vllm-openai:ec-cpu-connector-support`,
  Encode Disaggregation guide). The component already adds the `USER=llm-d`
  workaround for vllm-project/vllm#44548, so the inline copies are removed.
- **`imagePullPolicy: Always`:** the `gpu-vllm/nightly` component now sets it on the
  vLLM container. `:nightly` moves every day, and with `IfNotPresent` a node that
  cached an older nightly runs a different vLLM build. In a live E/PD test, one encode
  pod ran vLLM 0.28.1 from a cached image while the other pods ran 0.29.1. The EC
  connector compatibility check includes the vLLM version.
- **`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`:** set only on instances that have
  `--ec-transfer-config`, because `ECCPUConnector` raises `ValueError` without the V2
  model runner:
  - Coordinator guide: encode, prefill
  - E/P/D: encode, prefill
  - E/PD: encode, decode
- **EC config:** P2P NIXL mode (`"ec_enable_nixl": true`). `ec_cpu_bytes`, which is
  required and has no default, replaces `num_ec_blocks`. The sizes keep the earlier
  capacity (Qwen3-VL-32B uses 40,960 bytes per encoder token):

  | Instances | Before | `ec_cpu_bytes` | Blocks | `/dev/shm` |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | E/P/D encode, E/P/D prefill, E/PD encode | `num_ec_blocks: 1000000` | 40 GiB | 1,048,576 | 90Gi |
  | E/PD decode | default (100,000) | 4 GiB | 104,857 | 20Gi |
  | Coordinator encode, prefill | default (100,000) | 4 GiB | 104,857 | 8Gi |

- **Docs:** each `--ec-transfer-config` has a comment that links to
  https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/ec_cpu_connector/.

### Coordinator Disaggregation guide

- **`--enable-scale-out` on all model servers:** `vllm serve` serves `/render`,
  `/derender` and `/inference/v1/generate` only with this flag
  (vllm-project/vllm#55176 replaced `VLLM_ENABLE_SCALE_OUT_ENDPOINTS` with it).
  Prefill needs it for render. All roles need it because the Coordinator sends
  `/inference/v1/generate` to every phase for `/inference/v1/generate`, Responses
  and Messages requests.
- **Render Service (`render/`, new):** render (`/v1/*/render`) is CPU-only work in
  the vLLM API server, so any vLLM instance that serves the model can handle it.
  Before this change, all render calls went to one `vllm launch render` sidecar in
  the Coordinator pod. llm-d/llm-d-router#2701 (fixes llm-d/llm-d-router#2696) adds
  render balancing across discovered endpoints, but only for the EPP
  `token-producer`. The Coordinator's `render` step still takes one `address`. So
  this guide spreads the render load with a Service: `coord-disaggregation-render`
  fronts the prefill pods on their `modelserver` port, and render capacity grows
  with the prefill replicas. The render step address is
  `http://coord-disaggregation-render.${NAMESPACE}.svc:8000`. The `.svc` suffix
  matches `NO_PROXY` in `multimedia-downloader/patch-coordinator-ca.yaml`, so render
  calls do not go through the media proxy.
  - Prefill only, not all vLLM pods: render on decode slows token streaming.
    Encode sets no `--max-model-len`, so render there accepts prompts that prefill
    and decode reject. Prefill returns one token per request, so its API server has
    spare CPU.
  - The `vllm-render` sidecar (`vllm-openai-cpu:v0.26.0`) and its volumes are
    removed. Render now runs on the same vLLM version as the model servers, and no
    extra copy of the model is downloaded.
- **Coordinator image:** `ghcr.io/llm-d/llm-d-router-coordinator:main` now uses
  `imagePullPolicy: Always`, because `:main` moves with every merge to llm-d-router
  main.
- **README:** step 2 applies `render/`, Cleanup deletes it, and the image note
  describes the nightly image and the EC settings.

### Encode Disaggregation guide

- **CoreWeave overlays (new):** `e-pd/coreweave` and `e-p-d/coreweave` add
  `rdma/ib: "1"` to each role. `rdma/ib` is removed from the E/P/D base decode and
  prefill patches, so the base and GKE overlays no longer request it. The README
  lists `coreweave` as a provider.
- **README:** describes the nightly image, the V2 model runner and the P2P NIXL
  settings. The GKE bullet no longer claims DRA and DRANet (RoCE), because the GKE
  overlays do not configure RDMA yet.

## Defaults

- `--enable-scale-out`: off in `vllm serve` when not set. Set only in the
  Coordinator guide. The multimodal guides do not use the scale-out endpoints and
  keep the default. vLLM builds from before 2026-09-14 do not know the flag.
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER`: not set on decode in the Coordinator guide and in
  E/P/D. vLLM then uses V2 by default (vllm-project/vllm#53183) and falls back to V1
  when a feature needs it.
- `ec_cpu_bytes`: required, with no default. vLLM does not check it against the
  `/dev/shm` size, so each value is below its pod's `/dev/shm` limit.
- `imagePullPolicy`: Kubernetes uses `IfNotPresent` when it is not set and the tag is
  not `:latest`. It is now `Always` on the vLLM container in every guide that uses
  `gpu-vllm/nightly` (E/PD decode and wide-EP GLM-5.2 already set it) and on the
  Coordinator.
- Render step `address`: no default in the Coordinator. It is now the Service URL.

## Testing

- [x] `kustomize build` passes for the Coordinator model servers (`base`,
  `coreweave`, `gke`), `coordinator/` and `render/`, and for E/PD and E/P/D
  (`base`, `coreweave`, `gke`). All 38 kustomizations that use `gpu-vllm/nightly`
  build, and the only change there is `imagePullPolicy: Always`.
- [x] Checked the built manifests. Every Deployment uses
  `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`. No env var name is duplicated. The V2 runner
  is set only on EC instances. The render Service selects only prefill pods. The
  render address host matches `NO_PROXY`.
- [x] Deployed E/P/D on CoreWeave and sent an image request. The encode pod logged
  `EC save`, `serving NIXL READ request` and `NIXL READ completed`, and prefill
  answered. A text-only request skipped encode.
- [x] Deployed E/PD on CoreWeave and sent an image request. The encode pod logged
  `NIXL READ completed`, and decode answered.
- [x] Deployed the Coordinator guide on CoreWeave (3 EPPs) and sent a text and an
  image request through the Gateway. Render went through `coord-disaggregation-render`
  to a prefill pod (`/v1/chat/completions/render` 200, 83 tokens, 1 image), and the
  encode pod logged `NIXL READ completed`. Both requests returned 200.

## Notes

- The Service balances connections, not requests. For more render capacity, add
  prefill replicas or CPU. llm-d/llm-d-router#2701 balances render per request, but
  only in the EPP. If the Coordinator's `render` step gets a similar option, it can
  replace this Service.
- The `ec_cpu_bytes` sizes depend on the model. For another model, calculate
  `out_hidden_size * (1 + deepstack layers) * dtype bytes` per token.
- GKE RDMA: the E/PD, E/P/D and Coordinator GKE overlays do not configure RDMA yet,
  so the NIXL KV-cache and encoder-cache transfers use TCP on GKE. We will open a
  follow-up issue to add the `gke-rdma` DRA component (one GPU+NIC claim per TP rank),
  as in the P/D Disaggregation guide, once it can be tested on a GKE A3/A4 cluster
  with DRA and DRANet.

title: Add remaining-work routing variant to the P2P KV-cache-sharing guide [Experimental]
body:
Adds a variant guide under `guides/p2p-kv-cache-sharing/remaining-work-routing/`, linked from the parent P2P guide's variant sections.

The variant routes long-context follow-ups by their remaining prefill work instead of their total length: a request whose prefix is pullable over the P2P tier counts only its fresh tail, so it runs on a short-work prefill class and pulls the prefix instead of queueing behind cold long prefills. Prefill classes split by the `llm-d.ai/prefill-work-range` label; the boundary is derived from deployment measurements (peak per-rank prefill throughput plus the pull cost model) by the included `calibrate_work_boundary.py`, which also emits the labels and EPP parameters as one consistent set.

Contents: deploy manifests (GLM-5.2-FP8, 3x DP8 engines), router configuration for the baseline and remaining-work EPPs (one-parameter difference), the calibration script, the benchmark harness, and measured results on agentic traces (C64: migration-eligible TTFT p50 -53%, and -33% on top of an engine-side `--long-prefill-token-threshold` baseline).

Marked [Experimental]: the EPP side depends on llm-d-router#2559 (issue llm-d-router#2540), still in review, and the split-pool premise is scale-dependent - at two prefill engines an undivided pool with prefix-affinity scoring can outperform the split; the guide targets deployments that require work-class separation.

Relates to: llm-d-router#2540, llm-d-router#2559.

title: fix(guides): unify PROVIDER_NAME default to none
body:
`guides/optimized-baseline` and `guides/modelexpress-p2p` documented different defaults for `PROVIDER_NAME`, the value passed to `--set provider.name=` in the router gateway install. PR #2260 changed the optimized-baseline README default to `none` inside the rendered `guide:env.static` block. Both `guide.yaml` files, the render source of truth, still said `gke`, so `scripts/guide.py render` would have reverted the README.

Both guides default `PROVIDER_NAME` to `none`, matching the router chart's default for `provider.name`. GKE users must set `PROVIDER_NAME=gke`: with `none`, the chart omits the `HealthCheckPolicy`, the load balancer health check fails against vLLM, and requests return 503. Each `guide.yaml` carries a comment above the variable stating the requirement, and each README states it in prose above the env block.

Related fixes in the same files:

- optimized-baseline `guide.yaml` declares `ROUTER_CHART_VERSION`. The variable existed only in the README's rendered block, so `guide.py render` deleted it and `render --check` failed on `main`.
- `guides/recipes/router/README.md` documented `provider.name=<gke|istio|none>`. The placeholder lists all four accepted values, and a paragraph describes what each value renders.

Seven other guide READMEs export `PROVIDER_NAME=gke` without a warning; a follow-up issue should track that sweep.

**Verification:**

- `scripts/guide.py check` and `scripts/guide.py render --check` pass for both guides.
- The scheduled GKE nightlies for both guides use `gateway_class: epponly` (standalone mode), which does not read `PROVIDER_NAME`, so the default change does not affect CI.

Fixes #2330

title: fix(wide-ep-lws): serve render endpoints on precise prefill pods
body:
Fixes #2439.

The `wide-ep-lws` precise variant fronts the prefill pods with a Service that owns no pods of its own and forwards `/v1/*/render` for the EPP `token-producer`. vLLM serves those scale-out endpoints only when `VLLM_ENABLE_SCALE_OUT_ENDPOINTS=1` ([vllm-project/vllm#54579](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54579), merged 2026-09-02, after v0.28.0), and this guide deploys `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`, so every render call returns 404.

The failure is silent: no request carries token IDs, the precise producer never runs and the index stays empty, but pods are `Ready`, the EPP holds all its KV-event subscriptions, and requests still return 200 from the remaining scorers. On a GLM-5.3 cell the same workload completed 2,269 requests with rendering broken against 2,853 with it working.

This sets the opt-in through a modelserver component applied by the precise overlay, on prefill only since that is what the render Service selects. Builds that predate the gate ignore the variable, so it is version-safe. The render manifests and the README no longer say that no model-server flag is needed, and the README's render verification step now says what a 404 there means.

`precise-prefix-cache-routing` uses the same podless Service pattern but pins a released image that predates the gate, so it is unaffected today and left alone.

### Verification

- `kubectl kustomize modelserver/gpu/vllm-glm-5.2/deployments/p2w1d1w1-precise` puts the variable on the prefill LeaderWorkerSet only, not on decode, which matches the Service selector.
- The 404 and a working render path were observed live on a GLM-5.3 wide-EP cell. The opt-in itself is from vLLM's route registration and renderer docs, not run, since that cell is torn down.

### Known follow-ups, not in this PR

- Tokenization runs only on prefill rank 0. Fronting decode as well needs a shared port name across roles, since decode's `8000` is the routing sidecar whose catch-all returns unknown paths to the gateway rather than the local engine.
- The `kv-events` component patches decode too, but the decode profile has no prefix producer, so those events only consume per-key LRU capacity and ingestion CPU.

Note that [vllm-project/vllm#55176](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55176) proposes replacing the variable with an `--enable-scale-out` flag, so this may need revisiting.

title: release branch updates for release 0.10
body: cc @llm-d/release-crew

title: never-run badges
body:
Seed a grey `never run` badge for every cell of the Release Testing matrix, so a
freshly cut release branch renders a readable table instead of a grid of broken
images.

## Problem

Every cell of the [Release Testing matrix](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/release/README.md#release-testing)
is a live shields.io endpoint pointing at `badges/<badge_name>_<release-branch>.json`
on `gh-pages`. That is what lets a single lane re-run update the table with no
re-render, and it should stay that way.

Shields has no default-if-missing, though. A cell whose endpoint file does not
exist renders the literal text `custom badge: resource not found` — there is no
such thing as an empty cell. #2590 says as much in its own description: *"a cell
showing an error badge means that lane has not published a badge for this release
yet."*

So a release branch starts as a table of broken images and stays partly broken
until every lane has been dispatched at least once. Measured against
`release-0.10` today:

| | count |
| --- | --- |
| cells in the matrix | 50 |
| `_release-0.10` badge files on `gh-pages` | 39 — all `"message": "dry-run"` |
| cells rendering `resource not found` | **11** |

There is a second, subtler problem visible in that table. Because `dry-run` is
the cheapest badge to produce, it is currently doubling as a placeholder — which
loses the distinction between *"we exercised this lane and the guide resolved
cleanly"* and *"nobody has touched this"*. Both read blue.

## What this does

`release-e2e.yaml` now seeds a placeholder for every badge the matrix references
before it dispatches anything:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "label": "VLLM GPU",
  "message": "never run",
  "color": "lightgrey"
}
```

Same field set and order as the heredoc in llm-d-infra's
`reusable-update-badge.yaml`, so a real run replacing a placeholder is a two-line
diff. `label` is copied from the lane's own `badge_label:` rather than recomputed,
so a cell's label does not change when the placeholder is replaced.

`lightgrey` is deliberately the same grey that reusable already writes for
`skipped` and `cancelled`: one consistent "no result" shade, distinguished by the
message rather than the colour.

### Three properties that are load-bearing

**Create-if-absent.** A placeholder must never overwrite a real result or a
deliberate `dry-run`. That is also what makes re-running free, which is why this
seeds on *every* dispatch rather than only the first.

**The full set, never the `lanes` subset.** The badge list comes from the same
`GUIDES` × `PROVIDERS` walk the sync scripts use, so it cannot drift from the
rendered table. Seeding only the matched lanes would leave every other cell
broken — the problem being fixed.

**One commit, not 50.** `gh-pages` is a Pages branch, and one push per badge
would mean ~50 Pages builds against a soft limit of about ten an hour. The
seeder builds a single tree via the Git Data API and updates the ref
**unforced** — losing the race to a lane's own push is better than clobbering it,
since `reusable-update-badge.yaml` pushes with no concurrency group and no retry.
On a rejected update it re-reads `gh-pages` and retries, which is what keeps it
create-if-absent: a badge written in between drops out of the next attempt. A
truncated tree listing is refused rather than guessed, because that would make
present files look overwritable.

## Changes

- **`scripts/seed-release-badges.py`** (new) — the seeder. Stdlib only, since
  `ci-guides-check.yaml` installs just `pyyaml` and `pytest`. Supports
  `--dry-run`.
- **`scripts/matrix_common.py`** — `badge_file_name()` extracted out of
  `badge_endpoint()` so the `_{matrix_type}` suffix rule (which has to agree with
  llm-d-infra or the matrices point at files nobody writes) exists in exactly one
  place; plus `_extract_badge_label()` and `matrix_badge_labels()`. The tuple
  `discover_workflows()` yields is unchanged — both sync scripts unpack it
  positionally.
- **`.github/workflows/release-e2e.yaml`** — one job becomes
  `validate` → `seed-badges` → `dispatch`.
- **`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/new-release.md`** — the outstanding-lane check had to
  change; see below.
- **`scripts/tests/test_seed_release_badges.py`** (new) — 30 tests, picked up by
  `ci-guides-check.yaml`, whose path filter now also covers the two scripts.

### Why validation became its own job

Seeding must not run before `release_branch` has been checked, and it needs
`contents: write`, which the dispatch step should not have. `badge_file_name()`
gives `nightly` no suffix, so a `--matrix-type nightly` slip would quietly write
placeholders over the **nightly** badges and blank out the Nightly Testing
matrix. Hence validation ahead of the write, a second independent guard inside
the script for hand runs, top-level `permissions` narrowed to `contents: read`,
and `contents: write` scoped to `seed-badges` alone.

### The release template's badge check had to change

The "which lanes are still missing" step used
`comm -23 /tmp/expected.txt /tmp/got.txt`, i.e. it detected lanes by the
**absence** of a badge file. Once every cell is seeded that returns nothing,
always. It is now a query over badge *contents*, printing every non-green cell
with the reason:

```text
fast-model-actuation-base-ocp                 never run
pd-disaggregation-ocp                         dry-run
```

`never run` for a lane nobody has dispatched, `dry-run` for one only exercised
without a stack, a failure category for one that ran and failed, and `MISSING`
for a badge the seeder did not create — which now means the matrix has a broken
cell and the `seed-badges` job needs a look.

Also corrected two stale counts in that template and in the workflow header:
there are **50** lanes and 50 distinct badge names, one per cell, not "42 names
for 43 lanes".

## Verification

- `pytest scripts/tests/` — 68 pass (30 new).
- yamllint, actionlint and markdownlint clean at the pinned pre-commit versions.
- `sync-nightly-matrix.py --check` in sync, and `release/README.md` is
  byte-identical after the `matrix_common` refactor — no badge URL moved.
- The matrix-type guard rejects `nightly`, `main`, `release-0.99.1` and `""`
  before any API call.
- A test asserts the seeded badge set equals the set
  `sync-release-matrix.py` actually renders, so the two cannot drift.
- Live `--dry-run` against `gh-pages`: **would seed 11 of 50 (39 already
  present)** — the same 11 cells independently confirmed to be rendering
  `resource not found`.

Nothing has been written to `gh-pages` yet.

### After merge

Dispatch `release-e2e.yaml` with `release_branch=release-0.10`,
`list_only=true`. Expect one commit on `gh-pages` adding 11 files, a step summary
reporting 11 seeded / 39 present, zero lanes dispatched, and the `release-0.10`
section rendering 50 badges with no `resource not found` — 39 blue `dry-run`,
11 grey `never run`.

## Out of scope

`reusable-update-badge.yaml` lives in llm-d-infra and pushes to `gh-pages` with
no concurrency group and no retry. This PR works around that rather than fixing
it; the seeder's retry loop is the workaround.

title: feat(observability): wire metric-to-trace navigation for EPP exemplars
body:
Closes #2462.

The EPP attaches trace IDs to `llm_d_epp_request_duration_seconds` as Prometheus exemplars (llm-d/llm-d-router#2774), but nothing in the recipe made them usable. Three things were missing, and none of them error when absent - the exemplar just quietly isn't there:

- `enableFeatures: [exemplar-storage]` - without it Prometheus parses the exemplar off the scrape and drops it
- a Jaeger datasource in Grafana - the tracing script installs Jaeger, the prometheus script only registered Prometheus, so the exemplar had nowhere to point
- `exemplarTraceIdDestinations` on the Prometheus datasource - without it `trace_id` renders as plain text instead of a link

The values file is written twice, once per mode, so all three go into both branches. The TLS branch already wrote its own `jsonData`; both settings are now built into a single block, because two `jsonData` keys under one datasource is valid YAML in which one silently wins.

The link is written twice. Grafana's datasource link sends a TraceQL query, which the Jaeger datasource answers with "No data", so a URL link straight to the Jaeger UI goes first. It defaults to `http://localhost:16686`, the port-forward the tracing docs use, and `JAEGER_UI_URL` overrides it.

Jaeger is optional and its namespace is chosen at install time, so the link is wired only when a `jaeger-collector` service is found, with `TRACING_NAMESPACE` to override.

The only dashboard change is `"exemplar": true` on the P99 query of the existing latency panel. All three quantiles read the same buckets, so enabling them all would draw the same points three times.

**Verifying**

`scripts/test-prometheus-exemplar-config.sh` runs the real installer against stubbed kubectl/helm - no cluster needed - and asserts on the values file helm would actually receive. 55 assertions over seven configurations: no tracing installed, central mode, central + TLS, individual mode, explicit `TRACING_NAMESPACE`, explicit `JAEGER_UI_URL`, and a `TRACING_NAMESPACE` holding no Jaeger.

End to end, @gyliu513 ran the recipe with an EPP built from llm-d/llm-d-router#2774 and confirmed clicking an exemplar on the latency panel lands on the trace in Jaeger.

title: fix(makefile): restore the leading tab on the uninstall-docker completion message
body:
`Makefile:165` starts at column zero, so make does not read it as part of the `uninstall-docker` recipe.

The line contains a colon, in `Remove alias if set:`, so make reads it as a rule rather than reporting a missing separator. The file parses with no warning.

## Two consequences

The recipe ends at line 164, so the completion message never prints:

```
$ make -n uninstall-docker | tail -1
podman stop llm-d-container && podman rm llm-d-container
```

`install-docker` at `:154`, `uninstall-k8s` at `:187` and `uninstall-openshift` at `:215` all print theirs, at `:157`, `:195` and `:224`. This is the only one that does not.

And make defines a target out of the text:

```
$ make -p -n | grep '^@echo'
@echo: unalias llm-d"
```

## After

```
$ make -n uninstall-docker | tail -1
echo "podman uninstallation complete. Remove alias if set: unalias llm-d"

$ make -p -n | grep -c '^@echo'
0
```

`CONTAINER_TOOL` is auto-detected, so these runs show `podman`. The same holds for `docker`.

## The repository already states the rule

`.editorconfig`, added in #2103:

```
# Makefiles require tabs
[Makefile]
indent_style = tab
```

## Scope

One character. A scan of the whole file for a column-zero line inside a recipe block returns line 165 and nothing else. The only other hits are `:250` to `:260`, the space-indented prerequisite continuation under `check-tools`, which is correct as written.

`make uninstall-docker` was run with `-n` only. Running it for real stops and removes a container.

`make help` and `make verify` both exit 0, so the file still parses.

## Duplicate search

`gh issue list --state all` for `Makefile tab` and for `uninstall-docker`, and `gh pr list --state all` for `Makefile`, return nothing covering this. This is still the only open pull request touching the `Makefile`.

#2339 has since merged, as `4403300`. It renamed `$(PROJECT_NAME)` to `$(IMAGE_REGISTRY_REPO)` and moved the recipe, and it kept the column-zero start, so the line numbers above are its numbers and this branch is rebased on top of it.

title: fix(smoke-test): keep the real /v1/models status in the summary table
body:
`check_models` discards the status it has just reported. `helpers/smoke-test/healthcheck.sh:184` fails with the real code, and `:185` overwrites it with `000`, which is the sentinel `curl` produces when nothing answered at all.

So a reachable endpoint returning 503 reads as unreachable in the summary table, while the failure list directly below it shows the true code. Both come from the same variable in the same run:

```
║  /health          HTTP 503               ║
║  /v1/models       HTTP 000   count=-     ║
║  /v1/chat/completions HTTP 503   8     ms   ║
...
Failures:
  - /v1/models returned HTTP 503
  - /v1/chat/completions returned HTTP 503
```

`/health` and `/v1/chat/completions` both report 503 correctly. `/v1/models` is the outlier.

Every other exit from this code keeps the status: `check_health` at `:171`, and `check_models` itself at `:194` and `:210`. This is the only path that loses it.

## The change

Reporting `${http_code}` covers both cases, because `curl` already yields `000` when the connection fails. Verified against a 503 server and against a port nothing listens on:

```
=== 503 server ===
║  /v1/models       HTTP 503   count=-     ║
=== nothing listening ===
║  /v1/models       HTTP 000   count=-     ║
```

The sentinel survives where it is real, and the true code survives where there is one.

## Test

`tests/test_healthcheck_failure.py` already stands up a `ThreadingHTTPServer` answering 503 to everything, but asserted only the exit code, the `UNHEALTHY` banner and the word `failed`. It now also asserts the row.

```
$ python -m pytest helpers/smoke-test/tests/
1 passed

$ shellcheck -x --severity=warning helpers/smoke-test/healthcheck.sh
(exit 0)
```

Revert the script, keep the test, and it fails on the new assertion.

## Not checked

`report_json` at `:373` reads the same `MODELS_RESULT` and is affected identically, but this run did not exercise `-o json`.

## Duplicate search

`gh issue list --state all` and `gh pr list --state all` over `healthcheck.sh`, `smoke-test healthcheck` and `v1/models HTTP 000` return only #2401, which fixed the subshell counter accounting in this same file and merged on 2026-08-30, and #767, the original addition. Nothing covers this.

title: fix(scripts): detect env vars nested in defaults in lint-envvars
body:
## Problem

`scripts/lint-envvars.py` enforces the rule in `scripts/ENVVARS.md` that every
variable a script references must be declared in its header. It misses any
variable that appears inside the default of another expansion, such as
`${A:-${B}}` or `${A:-$B}`.

`find_used_vars` matches `${NAME...}` all the way to the first closing brace.
For `${A:-${B}}` that match ends at the inner `}`, so `B` is swallowed by the
outer match and never recorded as used.

The effect is that a script can reference an undeclared variable and still pass
the lint, whenever that reference appears only in a nested default.

## How to reproduce

```bash
cat > /tmp/nested.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Required environment variables:
# - A: declared in the header

echo "${A:-${B}}"
EOF

python3 scripts/lint-envvars.py /tmp/nested.sh
```

Before (`main`), exit code 0 even though `B` is not declared:

```text
✓ Checked 1 script(s) - all environment variables properly declared
```

After this change, exit code 1:

```text
/tmp/nested.sh: Undeclared environment variables:
  - B

✗ 1 error(s) found
```

## The change

One line in `find_used_vars`: match only the opening `${NAME` instead of
matching through the closing brace. Nested references then show up as their own
matches. Every reference that matched before still matches; the new pattern
only finds more.

I also added `scripts/tests/test_lint_envvars.py` (6 tests), in the same style
as `test_lint_dockerfile_envvars.py`. It covers plain forms, a braced and a bare
nested variable, a composed default like `${V:-cu${CUDA_MAJOR}${CUDA_MINOR}}`,
and end-to-end `lint_script` checks for both the failing and passing case.

## Impact on existing scripts

None today. `docker/scripts/cuda/runtime/install-vllm.sh` uses this pattern
(`${VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_COMMIT:-${VLLM_COMMIT_SHA}}`), but `VLLM_COMMIT_SHA`
is also referenced directly elsewhere in that script, so it was already caught.
This closes the gap for the case where a variable appears only in a nested
default.

## Testing

- New tests pass with the change, and 4 of the 6 fail without it (the other 2
  are controls for plain and correctly declared cases).
- `python -m pytest scripts/tests/`: 45 passed, 1 skipped (the same skip as
  before this change).
- `scripts/lint-envvars.py` over all 13 scripts matched by the pre-commit
  hook (`docker/scripts/**/*.sh`): still passes, no new failures.

title: feat(workload-autoscaling): add AMD ROCm deploy script for the KEDA+EPP nightly
body:
## Summary

Adds the deploy script for the AMD ROCm KEDA + EPP autoscaling nightly and turns on its schedule. The workflows come from #2582, which this PR includes until it merges.

## What the script does

It deploys the ROCm optimized-baseline model server, the EPP router and the keda-epp `k8s-queue` ScaledObject in one namespace, following `nightly-deploy-ocp-keda-epp.sh`. On top of the overlay it:

- retargets the ScaledObject at the ROCm decode Deployment
- points both triggers at the cluster's Prometheus, found from the Prometheus CR
- caps replicas at 2 and shortens scale-down to 60s so the validator sees it within the run
- pins the router chart to v0.9.0, as the OCP lane does, because of llm-d-router#1681

Before finishing, it checks that Prometheus has the exact series both triggers query. KEDA reads a query with no series as 0, so a wrong label or an unscraped EPP would otherwise leave the ScaledObject Ready but unable to scale. The Fallback check in the OCP script does not catch this, because the base ScaledObject sets no `spec.fallback`.

## Schedules

The nightly runs at 18:00 UTC and the status roll-up at 20:00 UTC, clear of the other ROCm nightlies.

## Test plan

Ran the script and `e2e-validate.sh --extra-validate scale-event` on MI355X the way the workflow invokes them.

- Deploy passed and both series were present in Prometheus
- `e2e-validate.sh` passed 10/10 through the EPP
- Under the burst KEDA scaled from 1 to 2 replicas, then back to 1
- A wrong EPP service label and an unreachable Prometheus both fail the deploy with a clear error
- A second run in the same namespace passes, and teardown leaves no namespace, Helm release, cluster RBAC or ScaledObject

The burst scales on running requests. The queue trigger stays at 0 at this load, as on the OCP lane.

## Related

- CI half: #2582
- Guide: `guides/workload-autoscaling/keda-epp/README.md`

title: fix(pd-disaggregation): use kv_consumer for TPU v6 decode
body:
vLLM defines KV roles as overlapping sets, so kv_both sets is_kv_producer=True. 
TPUConnector collapses the roles into a single is_producer flag and returns early in get_num_new_matched_tokens when it is set, never consulting is_kv_consumer. With kv_both the decode engine reports zero loadable tokens on every request: prefill stages KV blocks that are never pulled and expire with "KV transfer timeout. 


Measured on TPU v6e (Qwen3-30B-A3B), kv_both -> kv_consumer:
  decode reqs_to_load:          0 -> 12
  decode insert_kv_chunks:      0 -> 3 per 3 reqs
  prefill KV transfer timeouts: every request -> 0
  avg transfer size:            0 -> 420-810 MB

   `uses:` llm-d-infra's `reusable-ci-nightly-benchmark.yaml` and passes the eval
   as the **workload** (`harness: eval-containers`), the same way
   `inference-perf` is the workload for the perf nightlies. Runs at `0 2 * * *`,
   clear of the 03:00 slot the other eight OCP nightlies share.

### Why the eval complements inference-perf rather than duplicating it

The guide's existing templates report throughput, TTFT, and ITL — how fast the
stack serves a synthetic agentic load. This one drives a **real coding agent**
(aider-polyglot) and reports **reward**: the fraction of tasks actually solved.
The guide's own Benchmarking section already named that as a gap — *"Replaying
complete agent dependency graphs with tool timing and sub-agent fan-out remains a
separate evaluation mode."*

The two modes catch different failures. A broken tool-call parser, reasoning
traces leaking into content, or truncation mid-solution each leave TTFT and ITL
perfectly healthy while the agent silently fails every task. Reward sees them: a
uniform 0.0 across tasks points at a transport or parser fault, a spread reflects
genuine task difficulty.

Unlike its siblings the template takes `${MODEL}` rather than pinning a handle,
because the harness resolves the served model from the deployment itself
(`EVAL_MODEL="${LLMDBENCH_DEPLOY_CURRENT_MODEL:?}"`). One template therefore
covers Nemotron-3-Ultra, GLM-5.2, Qwen3-Coder-480B, and smaller models where a
cheap repeatable signal matters more than frontier scale.

### Revised from the dispatch approach (thanks @maugustosilva)

The first version of this PR used a cross-repo `workflow_dispatch` into
llm-d-benchmark, on the grounds that the shared engine couldn't drive the eval.
That's no longer true, and the review was right to push back:

- `--cluster-config` and `-j` were missing from the engine. **llm-d-infra#244
  has since merged** and adds both (`cluster_config`, `tasks`).
- `eval-containers` is already a declared value of the engine's `harness` input,
  and `workload/harnesses/eval-containers-llm-d-benchmark.sh` is in
  llm-d-benchmark on `main`.

With those in place a separate dispatch path buys nothing, so this revision
**deletes** `EVAL_DISPATCH_TOKEN`, the `github-script` dispatch, and the
run-URL polling — about 85 lines. A reusable-workflow call needs no PAT, and the
run now shows up as a normal job in this repo instead of a link to another one.

### The anyuid SCC is a prerequisite, not a CI step

My earlier argument was that the eval needs the **anyuid SCC** bound before
standup (the eval image and vLLM both run as root), and that putting an
OpenShift-specific SCC grant into the engine all nightlies share was too wide a
blast radius. The second half stands; the first half was wrong about where the
grant belongs.

`config/cluster-configs/examples/openshift-pokprod.yaml` already supplies the
`serviceAccount` and `runAsUser` to the cluster-generic scenario, and its own
header documents the binding as a **one-time-per-namespace prerequisite**:

```
oc create serviceaccount eval-runner -n llm-d-nightly-eval-containers-ibm-gpu
oc adm policy add-scc-to-user anyuid -z eval-runner -n llm-d-nightly-eval-containers-ibm-gpu
```

That's cluster state, not per-run work. It's recorded in the workflow header,
and the shared engine carries no OpenShift privilege logic.

### On the nightly's model

@maugustosilva — agreed on the direction, and this now uses the mechanism you
described, with the eval as the guide's workload.

The nightly serves **Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B on a single H100**, via
`config/scenarios/examples/eval-containers-aider-polyglot-gpu.yaml` — already on
llm-d-benchmark `main`, so there's no cross-repo dependency here. That model is
deliberate rather than a stand-in: a nightly wants a fast, cheap, every-night
signal, and this configuration scores non-trivially on aider-polyglot, so a score
regression is meaningful. The guide's three documented deployments are 64-GPU
configurations — right as reference deployments, but a nightly on that footprint
is a capacity event, not a regression test.

Worth stating plainly, since my first version of this PR got it wrong: nothing in
the guide scopes it by model size. There is no `gpu.product` selector or H200
constraint in the manifests, and the guide's substance — the routing and
scheduling profile in `router/agentic-serving-gpu.values.yaml` (prefix-cache
affinity, token-load scoring, prefill/decode filters) — binds to model servers by
label:

```yaml
  modelServers:
    matchLabels:
      llm-d.ai/guide: "agentic-serving-gpu"
```

`llm-d.ai/guide` and `llm-d.ai/model` are independent labels, so the guide's
identity is decoupled from the model by design.

The nightly drives the eval through the shared engine via `scenario_dir: examples`
against the eval's own scenario, which is what makes it self-contained: the
scenario is on llm-d-benchmark `main`, so nothing else has to land first. If this
guide later migrates to the `guide.yaml` method, the same job becomes
`scenario_dir: guides` + `standup_scenario: agentic-serving` by changing two
inputs, and the served model then comes from the guide's own manifests via the
engine's `--model` auto-detection.

### Cluster selection is by workflow name

Worth flagging for reviewers, since it's non-obvious: the engine picks the
cluster by grepping `github.workflow` for a provider substring
(`reusable-ci-nightly-benchmark.yaml:289-303`). `"OCP"` in the title selects the
self-hosted pok-prod runner pool and `KUBECONFIG_DATA_OCP`. So the
`(OCP GPU)` suffix and the `-ibm-` filename segment are load-bearing.

### Testing

- `actionlint` clean, and the full `pre-commit` suite passes on the new file
  (including `sync-nightly-matrix --check` — `eval-containers` is a workload,
  not one of the ten release-gating guides in `matrix_common.GUIDES`, so it's
  correctly absent from the matrix table).
- Every value in the `with:` block diffed against the engine's declared inputs.
  `scenario_dir: examples` and `workload: aider-polyglot.yaml` both resolve
  (`config/scenarios/examples/eval-containers-aider-polyglot-gpu.yaml`,
  `workload/profiles/eval-containers/aider-polyglot.yaml.in`).
- `decode_pods` is deliberately **not** exposed: the engine only applies it to
  kustomize `patch-*.yaml` manifests (step gated
  `if: env.LLMDBENCH_CICD_METHOD == 'kustomize'`), and this scenario stands up
  via `modelservice`, so the input would silently do nothing. Replica count
  lives in the scenario.
- Unlike the siblings, every input referenced in `with:` is declared or literal,
  so `actionlint` reports no `property "..." is not defined` warnings. The rest
  of the family has 535 of these; I didn't touch those files.

Not exercised: a live nightly, which needs the one-time SCC binding above on
pok-prod.

### Note on the DCO bot comment

The "Unsigned commits detected!" comment above is stale — it fired at 07:32:10
against an earlier push, 11 minutes before the signed commit landed. Both
commits on this branch are SSH-signed and report `verified: true` /
`reason: valid` from the commits API.

title: docs(observability): add WVA dashboards and alerts to llm-d
body:
## What this PR does

Moves the Workload-Variant-Autoscaler's user-facing observability assets into `llm-d/llm-d`, per the [observability-integration proposal](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/proposals/observability-integration.md) and #1983. This is the llm-d half of [wva#1466](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-workload-variant-autoscaler/issues/1466); the cleanup PR in the component repo follows once this lands, as that issue's acceptance criteria require.

It mirrors the layout the EPP migration established rather than inventing one — dashboards alongside the existing seven, the `PrometheusRule` as a sibling of `epp-alerting-rules.yaml`.

**Added:**

| File | Source in wva |
|---|---|
| `guides/recipes/observability/grafana/dashboards/llm-d-wva-operational.json` | `deploy/grafana/operational-dashboard.json` (16 panels) |
| `guides/recipes/observability/grafana/dashboards/llm-d-wva-benchmark-scaleup.json` | `deploy/grafana/benchmark-dashboard.json` (5 panels) |
| `guides/recipes/observability/alerts/wva-alerting-rules.yaml` | `config/components/prometheus-alerts/prometheusrule.yaml` (5 alerts) |

## The dashboards are not copied verbatim

This is the part worth reviewing closely. The two dashboards did not use this repo's datasource convention, and copying them across unchanged would have produced dashboards that load but don't bind:

- The operational dashboard bound every panel to a `$datasource_uid` template variable — a name that exists only in the wva repo.
- The benchmark dashboard had **no datasource variable at all** and no `uid` on its datasource references, relying on whatever Grafana had set as default.

Every dashboard already here uses `${DS_PROMETHEUS}` with a standard `datasource`-type template variable. Both files were retargeted — **47 datasource references in total** — and given that variable, so they behave like their neighbours. `load-llm-d-dashboards.sh` globs `*.json`, so no registration was needed.

I left the panel content, queries, and dashboard `uid`s untouched; the `uid`s are stable so existing links keep working.

## Alerts

Renamed to `wva-alerting-rules` and relabelled `app: wva-metrics`, matching `epp-alerting-rules.yaml`. The component repo used `release: kube-prometheus-stack`, which is a kube-prometheus-stack discovery convention rather than this repo's.

Worth noting: the `ruleSelector` caveat already documented in `alerting.md` Step 1 applies here identically — in central mode `ruleSelector: {}` picks up any rule, and in scoped mode neither this file nor the EPP one carries the `monitoring-ns` label. I have not changed that behaviour, only matched the existing precedent.

## Docs

- `alerting.md` — intro now covers both components, plus a WVA section with apply/verify steps and a reference table for the five `wva.rules` alerts. These fire on autoscaler health rather than request-path health, which the section calls out.
- `metrics.md` — the expected `kubectl get configmaps` output now lists the two new dashboards, so the sample stays accurate.

## What is deliberately not here

The ServiceMonitor and the `docs/user-guide/monitoring.md` runbook. I asked on [wva#1466](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-workload-variant-autoscaler/issues/1466) whether the scrape manifest belongs under `guides/workload-autoscaling/.../monitoring/` or in the shared recipe directory — the issue says "or equivalent recipe path" and I would rather match @gyliu513's intent than guess and have it moved twice. Happy to add both here once that's settled, or in a follow-up.

## Testing

Both dashboards parse as valid JSON and retain their panel counts; no `$datasource_uid` references remain. The `PrometheusRule` retains all five alerts across the single `wva.rules` group.

I have not applied these to a live cluster — I don't have a Grafana/Prometheus stack with WVA running to hand, so the datasource rebinding is verified by structure rather than by rendering. Worth a look from someone who can load them.

---

*Disclosure: prepared with AI assistance. The asset inventory, the datasource-convention mismatch, and the alert reference were checked against both repositories before writing.*

title: Slack notification workflow
body:
## What

Posts the result of every **scheduled** nightly to the Slack channel of the SIG that owns it, from within the repo instead of via the GitHub app for Slack.

Closes #1548.

## Why

The GitHub app for Slack (`/github subscribe`) hit two limits we could not work around: it only supports **one workflow subscription per channel** (so `#sig-router`, which owns 16 nightlies, could never be covered), and it **also fired on manual `workflow_dispatch` runs**.

## How

```
.github/slack-channels.yaml          <- source of truth (keyed by workflow FILE name)
        |  scripts/sync-slack-channels.py --fix  (generates the `workflows:` list)
        v
.github/workflows/notify-slack-nightly.yaml   <- GENERATED list, do not hand-edit
        |  at runtime
        v
.github/scripts/notify-slack-nightly.py       <- routes on workflow_run.path
```

Two identifiers, deliberately: the **trigger** must use display names because `workflow_run` matches on nothing else, which makes it the part that breaks *silently* — rename a nightly and notifications just stop, indistinguishable from a quiet night. Generating that list turns the rename red in the same PR. **Runtime routing** uses the workflow *file* name, which is stable, so a rename can only stop notifications, never misroute them.

A nightly in neither `channels` nor `skip` fails the new `sync-slack-channels` pre-commit hook — the only place the mistake can be caught, since an unrouted nightly is also absent from the trigger and therefore never fires at all.

**Routing**: 40 nightlies across 7 channels, 4 explicitly skipped with a reason (= all 44 `nightly-*.yaml`). `#sig-router` 16, `#sig-kv-disaggregation` 7, `#llm-d-intel` 6, `#sig-pd-disaggregation` 5, `#sig-autoscaling` 3, `#sglang-collab` 2, `#fast-model-actuation` 1. Note SGLang and Intel XPU route by engine/accelerator rather than by guide, because that is who acts on a failure. Run `python scripts/sync-slack-channels.py --audit` for the full table.

## Decisions worth a look in review

- **Only `schedule` runs notify** — the whole point of the change. The filter must live in the job's `if:`; `workflow_run` cannot filter on the upstream run's own event.
- **Re-runs of a scheduled run DO notify**, marked `(attempt N)`: when a SIG re-runs a nightly that failed on a transient cluster error, that result is the current truth about the guide.
- **`cancelled` / `skipped` do not notify.** Every nightly sets `cancel-in-progress`, so dispatching one mid-flight cancels the previous run — not news for a channel.
- **The guide's result comes from the `nightly` jobs, not the run conclusion.** `update-badge` runs with `if: always()`, so a green test whose badge push failed surfaces as a failed *run*; reporting that verbatim would tell a channel its guide is broken when it is not. That case gets its own `test passed, update-badge failed` message.
- **Unrouted at runtime → `#llm-d-ci-alerts` + warning, not a failed job.** A red notifier is a second alert channel nobody watches.
- Slack action **pinned by SHA**; `permissions` limited to `contents: read` + `actions: read`, which matters because a `workflow_run` workflow gets secrets and a privileged token even when the upstream run had neither.

## Files

New: `.github/slack-channels.yaml`, `scripts/sync-slack-channels.py` (`--check`/`--fix`/`--audit`, modelled on `sync-nightly-matrix.py` and reusing `matrix_common.py`), `.github/workflows/notify-slack-nightly.yaml`, `.github/scripts/notify-slack-nightly.py`.

Modified: `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (new hook), `.github/workflows/README.md` (new "Slack notifications" section + a third step in "Adding a new guide").

No nightly workflow is touched, and nothing is needed in `llm-d-infra`.

## Testing

Validated against real runs (success, failure, cancelled), including `32211600170`, which renders identically to what the GitHub app posted for it:

```bash
GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) python .github/scripts/notify-slack-nightly.py \
    --repo llm-d/llm-d --run-id <run-id> --dry-run
```
A real test can be seen in `#llm-d-ci-alerts` where the app has posted a filing workflow using:
```
  GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) .venv/bin/python .github/scripts/notify-slack-nightly.py \
    --repo llm-d/llm-d --run-id 32737554939 --channel '#llm-d-ci-alerts' --json \
  | curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
      -H 'Content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
      --data-binary @- | jq '{ok, error, channel}'
```
Plus 25 unit checks over the pure functions, all five guardrail failure modes verified to fail actionably and be fixed by `--fix`.

## Required before this takes effect

Needs Slack + repo admin; full checklist with an app manifest is in `.github/workflows/README.md`.

- [x] Create and install the Slack app with the **`chat:write`** bot scope
- [x] Create `#llm-d-ci-alerts` (fallback channel)
- [x] `/invite @llm-d-ci` in all 8 channels — skipping this is the likely first-deploy failure (`not_in_channel`)
- [x] Add the `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` repository secret

## Follow-ups

The 3 multimodal-serving nightlies need a SIG owner and a channel; they sit in `skip` until then. `nightly-build-image` is unrouted by design — happy to point it at a CI channel if reviewers prefer.

@llm-d/release-crew

title: feat(observability): add GKE TPU dashboard
body:
## Summary

The TPU PodMonitor added in #2190 provides a scrape recipe, but llm-d has no dashboard for inspecting the collected hardware metrics. This PR adds a GKE TPU overview dashboard and documentation for enabling it and diagnosing missing data.

- Show exporter scrape health, TensorCore utilization, HBM bandwidth utilization, and runtime duty-cycle and memory gauges when available.
- Reuse the shared dashboard loader and `${DS_PROMETHEUS}` convention. The dashboard selects a single exporter job using an exact match and filters hardware metrics with `make="cloud-tpu"`. It preserves per-instance and per-accelerator series instead of aggregating them. Panels show `No data` when a metric is unavailable.
- Document metric names, units, label scope, availability checks, and compatibility limits in the TPU recipe and observability reference.

The metric names and labels are based on the GKE device-plugin metrics consumed by [Ray's TPU metrics parser](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/blob/be4889928d3a396d7a1476d1bac3288dac72f9ab/python/ray/dashboard/modules/reporter/reporter_agent.py). The utilization metrics and their `make="cloud-tpu"` labels also appear in a [GKE v6e sample shared in a Ray issue](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/issues/57829).

ICI, PCIe, VPU, and kube-state-metrics topology recording rules remain follow-up work.

Relates to #2157

## Validation

- `make verify` passed.
- Markdown lint, JSON parsing, local documentation links, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local Prometheus 3.5.0 `promtool` checks passed: 34 dashboard query cases and six label-isolation cases using synthetic data. Coverage includes missing metrics, scrape failures, multiple instances, other component jobs, and foreign/missing `make` labels.
- As a negative control, replacing the exact job matcher with a regex matcher caused the label-isolation checks to fail.

The query checks were run locally; this PR adds no test tooling or CI dependencies. No live GKE/TPU deployment validation was available. The synthetic checks validate query behavior, not hardware metric availability.

Add COMPONENTS.md: core and ecosystem component roles
body:
## What

Adds `COMPONENTS.md`, defining two classes of component the project maintains:

- **Core** - on the inference request path; a failure or regression there
  degrades or breaks live inference. Deliberately small, carries production
  reliability expectations.
- **Ecosystem** - maintained and first-class, but not needed to serve a
  request (planning, benchmarking, analysis, simulation, adjacent services).

The role is orthogonal to graduation: a component moves from
`llm-d-incubation` into the main `llm-d` org and takes on one of the two roles
at that point. An ecosystem component can later be promoted to core if it moves
onto the request path and meets the higher bar.

## Why

Today "in the main org" is a single undifferentiated signal with no written
graduation criteria, so every graduation becomes an argument. This gives
committed-but-off-path components (starting with `llm-d-planner`) a real home
without implying request-path guarantees, while keeping the core set small and
high-bar to protect the request path.

## Notes

- Graduation criteria are grounded in the existing principles in `PROJECT.md`
- Includes a starter roster. The roster is the source of truth and changes by
  pull request.

| Data parallel size | 2 |
| Expert parallel size | 16 |
| RDMA NICs per node | 1 |

Each node runs one vLLM instance using TP8 across its eight local XPUs.
The two instances form DP2 across the two nodes. With expert parallelism
enabled, the model's experts are distributed across all 16 XPU ranks,
forming an **EP16 cross-node topology**.

```text
                       llm-d Router / EPP
                               |
                        Service port 8200
                               |
              +----------------+----------------+
              |                                 |
          Node 0 / LWS leader              Node 1 / LWS worker
          DP rank 0                        DP rank 1
          TP8: XPU 0-7                     TP8: XPU 8-15
          1 RDMA NIC                       1 RDMA NIC
              |                                 |
              +------ EP16 over XCCL/OFI -------+
                    allgather_reducescatter
```

Intel XPUs and RDMA network devices are allocated through Kubernetes
DRA using the gpu.intel.com and dranet-rdma DeviceClasses.

Changes
- Add the Qwen3-235B LeaderWorkerSet model server manifests.
- Configure vLLM with TP=8, DP=2, FP8 quantization, and expert
parallelism.
- Configure XCCL over OFI verbs for cross-node communication.
- Add DRA claims for eight Intel XPUs and one RDMA NIC per pod.
- Add an aggregated-serving EPP configuration targeting port 8200.
- Document the commands required to deploy the Qwen3-235B model and
its router configuration.
- Assign stable qwen-0 and qwen-1 hostnames to avoid ambiguous
hostname-prefix matching during oneCCL local-rank discovery.

title: fix(wide-ep): make Intel XPU decode manifest actually cross-node wide-EP
body:
## Problem

`decode.yaml` shipped with `leaderWorkerTemplate.size: 1` and only a `workerTemplate` (no `leaderTemplate`). Every "decode" pod was a fully independent TP+EP-only replica — no pod ever shared a DP/EP group with another pod. Despite the guide's name, expert parallelism was never actually organized across pods/nodes on the Intel XPU path.

## Fix

* `decode.yaml`: split into `leaderTemplate` (HTTP API + routing-proxy sidecar, DP-supervisor rank 0) and `workerTemplate` (`--headless`, exec-based probes). `leaderWorkerTemplate.size` bumped `1 -> 2` (smallest config that exercises real cross-pod EP). `vllm serve` args rewritten to the DP-supervisor pattern. Added `podAntiAffinity` (leader/workers on distinct hosts, scoped to this guide) and `rolloutStrategy` (avoids surge-based rollout deadlocks on capacity-constrained clusters).
* `prefill.yaml`: added the same `podAntiAffinity`/`rolloutStrategy`. `size` stays `1` — prefill scales via independent replicas, not a cross-node EP group; its own wide-EP is unvalidated and documented as such inline.
* `kustomization.yaml`: added a labels-transformer path for the new `leaderTemplate`.
* `router/xpu.values.yaml`: EPP endpoint selection now also requires `leaderworkerset.sigs.k8s.io/worker-index: "0"`, since headless decode workers share every other label with the leader but don't serve HTTP on port 8000.
* `README.md`: updated the Intel XPU config table and added notes on the fix and current EPLB status.

## Validation

Validated on a real 4-node/16-XPU Intel cluster: EP world size > 1 actually spans pods, correct expert split, cross-node P/D traffic (NIXL), and light concurrent request handling.

EPLB (expert-parallel load balancing) was not enabled as part of this fix; it's left as follow-up work for Intel XPU.

## Known gaps

* EPLB unsupported/unvalidated on Intel XPU (follow-up work).
* Not tested behind a Gateway/InferencePool front-end (direct Service routing only).
* Only tested with the small `DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` model, light concurrency only.
* `guides/wide-ep/monitoring` still assumes GPU-style `rank0..rank7` ports; pre-existing gap, not touched here.
* Prefill's own cross-node wide-EP (vs. replica scale-out) is unvalidated and out of scope.

title: fix(autoscaling): use plain HTTP for keda-epp generic-k8s prometheus scaler
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

The generic-Kubernetes KEDA autoscaling path in both keda-epp guides was broken. KEDA's prometheus scaler only applies a `TriggerAuthentication` CA when the trigger also sets `authModes` (its `GetAuthConfigs` returns early without it), so the shipped "CA-only" trigger silently fell back to the system trust store and failed serving-cert verification with `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. This path was never end-to-end tested against a real TLS Prometheus.

This PR reworks the generic-k8s path to plain in-cluster HTTP and preserves the (working) OpenShift path exactly:

- keda-epp-saturation and keda-epp-queue `k8s` overlays now target the bundled kube-prometheus-stack over plain in-cluster HTTP (`http://...:9090`) with no client auth, no `TriggerAuthentication`, and no CA secret.
- Removed the base `TriggerAuthentication` (deleted the saturation `base/triggerauthentication.yaml`; removed the embedded TA block from the queue `base/scaledobject.yaml`) and dropped the `deploy.prometheus_auth` step and the CA-secret cleanup from both `guide.yaml` files.
- OpenShift is unchanged: each guide now carries its own `ocp/triggerauthentication.yaml` (`authModes: bearer` + metrics-reader `service-ca.crt`), and the `ocp` overlay patches `serverAddress` to Thanos Querier and attaches it. `kubectl kustomize .../ocp` is byte-identical to `main` for both guides.
- Refreshed the README and `guide.yaml` prose, re-rendered both guides (`guide.py render --check` is clean), and added an `> [!IMPORTANT]` note documenting the KEDA CA/`authModes` caveat so future readers do not re-introduce a CA-only trigger.

Verified end to end on a kind cluster for both guides against a plain-HTTP Prometheus: the ScaledObject reaches `Ready=True`/`Active=True` with no `x509` errors, the generated HPA reads both external metrics over threshold, and the target Deployment performs a real 1-to-N scale-out.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Refs #2565

**Release note**:

```release-note
The generic-Kubernetes KEDA + EPP autoscaling guides (keda-epp-saturation, keda-epp-queue) now connect to the bundled Prometheus over plain in-cluster HTTP. The previous CA-only TriggerAuthentication never verified TLS on KEDA's prometheus scaler (it requires authModes to load the CA). The OpenShift path is unchanged and still uses bearer auth over HTTPS to Thanos Querier.
```

title: fix(workload-autoscaling): capture WVA controller diagnostics before CKS teardown
body:
Motivation:
The nightly CKS workload-autoscaling lane
(workload-autoscaling-cks-acc-gpu-vllm-x) has failed for at least seven
consecutive nights waiting for wva-controller-manager to become
Available. The root cause is unknown because the controller pod is
force-deleted during teardown before its state can be inspected —
kubectl describe output and pod logs never make it into the run output.

Approach:
Wrap the `kubectl wait deployment/wva-controller-manager ... --for=condition=Available`
step in nightly-deploy-cks.sh so that on failure, before the script exits
(and before the calling workflow tears the namespace down), it captures
and prints to stderr:
  - `kubectl describe` of the Deployment
  - `kubectl describe`, `kubectl logs --all-containers`, and
    `kubectl logs --all-containers --previous` (to catch a crashed prior
    container instance, e.g. CrashLoopBackOff) for every pod matching the
    wva-controller-manager- name prefix
This mirrors the existing diagnostics block later in the same script
(the KEDA fallback check), so it matches this file's own conventions.
nightly-deploy-ocp.sh's `kubectl wait` step does not have an equivalent
failure-diagnostics wrapper today — that parity gap is left for a
follow-up, since this PR only targets the CKS nightly lane the issue is
about. The script still exits 1 on failure, preserving the original CI
failure semantics.

This does not fix the underlying reason the controller never becomes
Available — that root cause is still unconfirmed and requires
inspecting a live CKS run. This change implements next step #1 from
the issue report ("Capture kubectl describe deploy/wva-controller-manager
plus the controller pod's events and logs before teardown runs") so the
next nightly failure leaves enough evidence in the run log to diagnose
the real problem.

Validation:
No live CKS/GPU cluster is available in this environment, so the
underlying Available-timeout failure itself could not be reproduced or
confirmed fixed (it isn't meant to be fixed by this change). What was
run:
  - `bash -n guides/workload-autoscaling/scripts/nightly-deploy-cks.sh` — passed.
  - `shellcheck -x --severity=warning guides/workload-autoscaling/scripts/nightly-deploy-cks.sh` — zero warnings.
    (Note: this repo's .pre-commit-config.yaml only runs the shellcheck
    hook against docker/scripts/*.sh, so this script is not gated by
    that hook; ran shellcheck manually as an extra check.)
  - Extracted the new diagnostic block into an isolated harness with a
    stubbed `kubectl` simulating the exact failure mode from the issue
    (kubectl wait returns 1, one matching pod
    wva-controller-manager-6bfcf4cfb5-qxvkw as in the issue's log
    excerpt). Confirmed: describe/logs/logs --previous output print in
    the correct order for the deployment and the matching pod, the
    pod-name grep matches correctly and is empty-safe under pipefail,
    and the script still exits 1, preserving the original failure path
    for the caller.

title: fix(no-kubernetes-deployment): enable EPP health checking for Envoy
body:
Fixes #2567

## What

The no-Kubernetes guide's `envoy.yaml` health-checks the EPP with `grpc_health_check` on the ext-proc port (`9002`). The EPP only serves `grpc.health.v1.Health` on that port when started with `--health-checking=true`, and neither EPP command in the guide passed it. Every check failed, Envoy held the EPP at `/failed_active_hc`, and requests reached it only through Envoy's panic routing.

This PR adds `--health-checking=true` to both EPP commands (container and from-source), which matches the router chart in priority-routing mode, where it passes the flag and fails the render if it's set to false (`routerlib/templates/_helpers.tpl`: *"priorityRouting requires EPP's gRPC health service on port 9002"*).

## Why it matters

With one EPP, completions succeed either way. That's why this went unnoticed. But:

- the health check the guide says it carries over from the standalone preset has never passed;
- a second EPP added for failover gets no health-based failover, because every EPP looks equally unhealthy and Envoy load-balances across all of them in panic mode.

| Envoy stat (`ext_proc` cluster) | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `health_check.success` / `failure` | 0 / 6 | 1 / 0 |
| `lb_healthy_panic` | 1 | 0 |
| `health_flags` | `/failed_active_hc` | `healthy` |
| completion via Envoy `:8081` | 200 | 200 |

Probing the EPP directly on main: port `9002` returns `UNIMPLEMENTED unknown service grpc.health.v1.Health`, and port `9003` returns `SERVING`.

## Changes

- `README.md`: `--health-checking=true` in both EPP commands; a paragraph on what it does and how it differs from `--grpc-health-port`; a `health_flags` check in **Verification**; the `failed_active_hc` symptom in **Troubleshooting**.
- `router/envoy/envoy.yaml`: a comment above `health_checks:` stating the requirement, since the guide tells users to copy this file to hosts on its own.

I considered dropping `health_checks` from `envoy.yaml` instead, but decided against it. The guide says it mirrors the standalone preset's health checks, and the health check is what makes a multi-EPP setup fail over.

## Testing

Ran the full guide on one host with Docker and 2 GPUs (RTX 3080 + RTX 3090). Two vLLM `v0.19.1` workers served Qwen3-0.6B, one per GPU, both listed in `endpoints.yaml`, behind EPP `main` and Envoy `distroless-v1.33.2`.

- [x] Before/after Envoy stats as in the table above; completions return 200 in both cases
- [x] `--health-checking` is present in the `v0.10.0` and `main` EPP images (`--help`)

- [x] `envoy --mode validate` passes on the edited `envoy.yaml`

title: pd-disaggregation: fold the TPU guide into the main guide, cache TPU weights on the node, pin TPU7x to vllm-tpu v0.26.0
body:
## Summary

Folds the separate TPU page of the P/D disaggregation guide into the main guide, and fixes two problems found while validating the TPU7x path end to end.

Three commits, each independently revertable:

1. **Fold the TPU guide into the main guide.** `README.tpu.md` was last synced with the shared content on 2026-06-12 and had drifted (dead benchmark anchor, retired `run_only.sh` flow, an env block that sourced `env.sh` before `REPO_ROOT` was set, an unflagged inheritance of the H200-calibrated `peakPrefillThroughput`). It is replaced by a `#### TPU` section next to `#### GPU`, with the dynamic sub-slicing content reduced to a pointer at `docs/infrastructure/providers/gke/dynamic-slicing/`. `README.tpu.md` and the orphaned `benchmark-templates/tpu.yaml` are deleted. The model-server overlays stay where they are; the nightly TPU workflow selects them by `accelerator_type`, and the other CI jobs discover work by path, so no CI change is needed.
2. **Cache model weights on the node for the TPU overlays.** Adds the node-local HuggingFace cache (`hostPath /var/cache/huggingface`, `HF_HOME`) already used by the GKE GPU overlays to the TPU base patches and the dynamic-slice manifests. Without it every container restart re-downloaded the 406 GB TPU7x model into the writable layer, which triggered ephemeral-storage eviction on nodes with other data on the boot disk. The boot-disk requirement is documented.
3. **Pin the TPU7x overlays to `vllm-tpu:v0.26.0`.** In `v0.27.0` through `v0.29.0` the vLLM scheduler reads `connector._kv_transfer_config` (`requires_kv_delivery`), but the bundled `TPUConnectorHMA` skips the base-class initializer, so EngineCore fails at startup with `AttributeError: 'TPUConnectorHMA' object has no attribute '_kv_transfer_config'`. Fixed upstream by vllm-project/tpu-inference#3566 (2026-09-12); no `vllm-tpu` release contains it yet. The shared `tpu-vllm/release` component stays at `v0.27.0` because tiered-prefix-cache's TPU multi-host offload (#2313) needs it; a new `tpu-vllm/release-v0.26.0` component pins only the two HMA overlays. The v6e overlay uses the non-HMA `TPUConnector` and is unaffected. This commit is reverted once a release includes the fix.

## Validation

* Deployed `modelserver/tpu/v7/vllm` from this branch on GKE TPU7x (`2x2x1`, 1 prefill + 1 decode, standalone router). `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions` succeed through the EPP; the prefill engine logs the KV send and the decode engine the KV pull for every request; decode reports 100% external prefix-cache hits (574/574 prompt tokens over three requests).
* Every `kustomization.yaml` under `guides/pd-disaggregation` builds; `tpu/v6/vllm` renders `v0.27.0`, both TPU7x overlays render `v0.26.0`.
* `make verify`, markdownlint (no new findings beyond the existing `<h4>`-in-`<summary>` pattern), yamllint, and the router `helm template` pass.
* Internal links and anchors in the changed Markdown resolve.

## Note

The regression in commit 3 was not caught by CI because the nightly TPU lane only runs `tpu/v6`. A TPU7x lane for the HMA path would close that gap after we can get capacity for nightly e2e test.

title: fix(ci): default harness_resources to 2/8Gi for Intel XPU nightly workflows
body:
## Problem
3 Intel XPU nightly workflows have been failing every run since 2026-09-09:
- `nightly-e2e-optimized-baseline-intel-acc-xpu-vllm-x`
- `nightly-e2e-pd-disaggregation-intel-acc-xpu-vllm-x`
- `nightly-e2e-precise-prefix-cache-routing-intel-acc-xpu-vllm-x`

```
Failed to deploy pod 'inference-perf-xxx': The Pod "inference-perf-xxx" is invalid:
spec.containers[0].resources.requests: Invalid value: "64Gi": must be less than or equal to memory limit of 8Gi
```

## Cause
- These workflows send `harness_resources=32/64Gi` to `llm-d-infra`'s reusable workflow, which only overrides the harness pod's memory **request** (`--set harness.resources.memory=64Gi`).
- Since `llm-d-benchmark#1882` (merged 2026-09-08), the memory **limit** comes from a separate field, `harness.resources.memoryLimit`, hard-coded to `8Gi` in the `intel-xpu` overlay used by these 3 scenarios.
- Result: `requests.memory=64Gi > limits.memory=8Gi` → Kubernetes rejects the pod → no harness pod → run fails.

## Fix
Default `harness_resources` to `2/8Gi` for these 3 workflows, matching the intel-xpu overlay's `memoryLimit`. This isn't an arbitrary downgrade — it's the value the overlay was originally sized for (single-node Kind/B60, harness sharing the node with the serving stack), and it ran successfully for weeks before `harness_resources` was introduced (see 8/18–8/27 run history, all green).

Other (non-XPU) nightly workflows are untouched — their overlays use the global default `memoryLimit=128Gi`, so `32/64Gi` doesn't conflict there. `predicted-latency-routing` / `wide-ep-lws` / `tiered-prefix-cache` on Intel XPU are also untouched — they don't set `accelerator.profile: auto`, so this overlay/bug doesn't apply to them.

## Scope
Stopgap only. Filing a follow-up issue on `llm-d/llm-d-infra` to also override `memoryLimit` alongside `memory`, so this can't recur for other accelerator overlays.

## What does this PR do?

Removes the explicit `image: REPLACE_MODEL_SERVER_IMAGE` line from `guides/multimodal-serving/e-disaggregation/modelserver/gpu/vllm/e-pd/base/patch-encode.yaml`.

## Why is this change needed?

The GKE e-disaggregation nightly fails with encode pods stuck in `InvalidImageName`:

```
spec.containers[modelserver]: Failed to apply default image tag "REPLACE_MODEL_SERVER_IMAGE": couldn't parse image name ...
```

Root cause is kustomize transformer ordering. In `e-pd/base/kustomization.yaml`, the encode skeleton comes from `recipes/modelserver/base/single-host/e-pd` and is filled in by `patch-encode.yaml`. Decode is unaffected because `patch-decode.yaml` carries no `image:` field, and e-p-d is unaffected because it ships encode as a full resource (substituted by the component, never re-patched).

With the image line removed, the encode container keeps the component-substituted image.

body:

After this change:

title: fix(observability): start P/D traffic statistics at zero
body:
## Summary

Initialize the P/D traffic generator statistics files as empty counters so an idle run reports zero requests.

## Root Cause

The statistics are calculated by counting lines in the counter files. The initial `echo "0"` writes one line to each file, so the generator reports one total, one successful request, and one failed request before any request has been sent.

## Changes

- Truncate the total, success, and failure counter files without writing an initial marker line.
- Add a regression test covering the initial statistics state.

## Reproduction

On the unmodified `main` branch, before sending any requests:

```text
1 1 1
```

After this change:

```text
0 0 0
```

## Validation

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q \
  scripts/tests/test_pd_traffic_stats.py
bash -n guides/recipes/observability/generate-traffic-pd.sh
shellcheck --severity=error -x \
  guides/recipes/observability/generate-traffic-pd.sh
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
```

All commands passed. The regression test reports `1 passed`.

## Scope

This only changes counter initialization. Per-request counter updates and final statistics aggregation are unchanged.
